info.title: What is Forest Bathing?
info.lead: Forest Bathing, or “Shinrin-yoku”, is the practice of spending slow, deliberate time in the forest with all five senses open. It is not a hike to conquer a summit — it is stopping, listening, smelling, touching, and letting the forest do its work on your body and mind.

points.title: Walk slowly
points.desc: Short distances over a long time. The point is what you notice, not how far you go.

points.title: Open your senses
points.desc: Listen to the forest, smell the soil and leaves, feel the bark and the wind.

points.title: Guided throughout
points.desc: A facilitator leads you through activities that connect you with nature along the way.

chet-kot.name: Chet Kot – Pong Kon Sao National Park
chet-kot.blurb: Forest inside a national park, about two hours from Bangkok. An overnight trip.

doi-tung.name: Doi Tung
doi-tung.blurb: Highland watershed forest in Chiang Rai. Cool year-round, with natural walking trails.

urban-bangkok.name: Urban Forest Bathing
urban-bangkok.blurb: Breathe with the forest. A mindful morning of Japanese forest bathing at Bang Krachao — Bangkok's green lung. Slow down, reconnect, and leave feeling lighter.
